reason: The winding drum needs its crank and ratchet to wind and hold the lifting cord.
expectation: The crank and ratchet will attach to the drum assembly.

effect: The drum and crank formed a hand winch, ready to install on the crane.
reaction: The explanation of the longer crank's trade-off was useful.
reason: The crane needs the winch to wind its lifting cord.
expectation: The hand winch will attach to the crane frame.

effect: The winch is installed, so the crane can now be fitted with its lifting cord.
reaction: That was a straightforward assembly step.
reason: The cord needs to connect the winch to the hook and pulley for lifting.
expectation: The cord and hook will be fitted to the crane.

effect: The lifting line is fitted, leaving the crane ready for its holding and stability parts.
reason: The pawl should engage the ratchet to hold a raised load, with the lever allowing release.
expectation: The holding and release mechanism will attach to the crane.

alternatives.reason: The ballast should also help stabilize the crane before testing.

effect: The pawl can hold the rope, but the crane still needs stability against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and stabilizing the crane is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help counterbalance a load before testing.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear of the crane.

effect: The ballast cannot be used yet, so the crane may need a test before it becomes relevant.
reaction: That was unexpected; I had thought the ballast would fit before testing.
reason: A padded test weight is a sensible first load for checking the rigged crane.
expectation: The crane will attempt to lift and hold the test weight.

effect: The test showed that the pawl holds the rope, but the crane tips; rear ballast is now the likely remedy.
reaction: The test made the distinction between holding and balance concrete.
reason: The rear ballast should counter the tipping revealed by the test.
expectation: The ballast will attach at the rear and help keep the crane's feet down.

effect: The ballast keeps the feet down in the supported low lift, and the pawl and release procedure are now clear.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the test lead to a stable crane.
reason: The crane has passed the low test and now needs to lift the cargo basket.
expectation: The crane will lift, hold and gently lower the basket.

effect: The basket test completed the goal: the crane lifted, held and gently lowered its load.
reaction: Seeing the pawl and careful release used in the final delivery was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the crane and correcting its tendency to tip made the difference between holding a rope and balancing a load concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the winch was straightforward but less informative than testing the completed mechanism.

surprise.text: The ballast could not be fitted before the test, even though its purpose seemed clear.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the tipping test before fitting the obvious ballast felt somewhat arbitrary, although the test demonstrated why it was needed.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the hands-on tests and explanations made the mechanisms worth exploring, especially when a test revealed a problem to solve.
